thesis: Reddit, Inc. (RDDT) operates a global community platform where users gather in topic-based forums ("subreddits") to share content, ask questions, and discuss interests. **[Fact]** The company monetizes primarily through advertising on its mobile apps and website, with additional revenue from data licensing and premium subscriptions. **[Fact]** FY2025 revenue was **$2.20 billion** (+69% versus FY2024 **$1.30 billion**), with net income **$529.7 million** after a **$(484.3) million** loss in FY2024. **[Fact]** Average daily active uniques ("DAUq") reached **126.8 million** in Q1 2026 (+17% year over year). Reddit went public in March 2024 and reports a single operating segment.
why_market_wrong: The market may be pricing Reddit as a mature social ad platform when monetization is still early. **[Fact]** Q1 2026 average revenue per unique ("ARPU") was **$5.23**, up **44%** year over year, while DAUq grew **17%**, showing yield expansion ahead of user growth. **[Inference]** Generalists may anchor on pre-2024 loss history or compare Reddit to Meta's scale, missing that Reddit's ad stack automation, vertical diversification, and data-licensing deals are still ramping. There is no dated catalyst; the inefficiency is **descriptive** (recent IPO, unproven moat at scale) rather than a timed equity yield curve setup.
